paraphrase: Brahman is bliss and consciousness; ignorance (avidyā) belongs to the individual selves, not to Brahman, and is of two kinds — non-apprehension (agrahaṇa) and misapprehension (anyathā-grahaṇa); it is neither Brahman's nature nor another real entity.
notes: Chapter-level (Brahmakāṇḍa); doctrinal content moderate, wording low.

original.text: āhur vidhātṛ pratyakṣaṃ na niṣeddhṛ vipaścitaḥ / naikatva āgamas tena pratyakṣeṇa virudhyate
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: The wise say perception is affirmative (it presents what is), not negating (it does not grasp difference); therefore scripture's teaching of oneness is not contradicted by perception.
The Upaniṣads do not have injunction (niyoga) as their purport, against the Prābhākara view; they make known the existent Brahman.

Knowledge from the Upaniṣadic sentence is not yet direct and does not by itself remove the deep-rooted impressions of difference; repeated contemplation (prasaṅkhyāna, upāsanā) of that knowledge makes it direct and removes them; works performed without desire help by purifying and assisting the rise of knowledge.
notes: Chapter-level (Siddhikāṇḍa and passim); the position is well attested through Maṇḍana's critics (Sureśvara, the Upadeśasāhasrī) and followers (Vācaspati).

paraphrase: The one called 'liberated while living' or 'of steady wisdom' is in truth an advanced seeker (sādhaka), not one fully freed, since full liberation comes only with the fall of the body.
notes: Reported position of Maṇḍana, low confidence; to be checked against the text.
